rubric_v1_gloss: “He who asserts his own views is not distinguished.” Ch. 22: “… from self-assertion, and therefore he is distinguished.”
source_scope: Laozi 24's second fault, with ch. 22's freedom from self-assertion.

teaching.quote: (So), he who displays himself does not shine; he who asserts his own views is not distinguished; … Hence those who pursue (the course) of the Tao do not adopt and allow them.
He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; from self-assertion, and therefore he is distinguished; …

limits: This does not ban stating views. The boundary between stating a view and asserting it is undecided in the source.

rubric_v1_gloss: “He who displays himself does not shine.” Ch. 22: “He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines.”
source_scope: Laozi 24's first self-display fault, with ch. 22's freedom from self-display.

teaching.quote: 24. He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm; … (So), he who displays himself does not shine; … Such conditions, viewed from the standpoint of the Tao, are like remnants of food, or a tumour on the body, which all dislike.
Therefore the sage holds in his embrace the one thing (of humility), and manifests it to all the world. He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; …

limits: The four faults overlap in ch. 24, so they are not exclusive types. Visibility imposed by a duty is not decided by the text.

rubric_v1_gloss: “He who is self-conceited has no superiority allowed to him.” Ch. 22: “… from self-complacency, and therefore he acquires superiority.”
source_scope: Laozi 24's fourth fault, with ch. 22's freedom from self-complacency.

teaching.quote: … he who is self-conceited has no superiority allowed to him. Such conditions, viewed from the standpoint of the Tao, are like remnants of food, or a tumour on the body, which all dislike.

He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; … from self-complacency, and therefore he acquires superiority. It is because he is thus free from striving that therefore no one in the world is able to strive with him.

limits: Legge uses 'self-conceited' in ch. 24 and 'self-complacency' in ch. 22. Accurate self-knowledge is not decided by the text.

rubric_v1_gloss: “He who vaunts himself does not find his merit acknowledged.” Ch. 22: “… from self-boasting, and therefore his merit is acknowledged.”
source_scope: Laozi 24's third fault, with ch. 22's freedom from self-boasting.

teaching.quote: … he who vaunts himself does not find his merit acknowledged; … Hence those who pursue (the course) of the Tao do not adopt and allow them.
He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; … from self-boasting, and therefore his merit is acknowledged; …

limits: This fault overlaps with self-display. Required reports or records are not judged by the text.
